content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm new to programming and would appreciate guidance on how to synchronize the time across multiple [product_name] modules on the same network. Any support is greatly appreciated. Thank you in advance.

Welcome to the forum. The approach depends on which [product_name] you are using. Older models can only synchronize time using a communication module. Newer versions, starting from [product_name] [version_no], support time synchronization via an NTP server.

Thanks for the warm welcome. As a beginner, I'm unsure how to set up NTP for these modules. The network doesn't have internet access; will this be an issue? All the modules are [product_name] [version_no].

Typically, an NTP server requires access to external time sources over the internet. If there's no internet, you can designate one [product_name] as the NTP server and set the others as clients, which will then synchronize with the server's time. Just make sure the server module maintains an accurate clock.
Thank you for responding so quickly! Are there any guides available for setting up one of the modules as the NTP server?
Please refer to the attached file for further instructions.
Fantastic! Thank you very much for your assistance.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is unsure about synchronizing time across several [product_name] modules on a local network, especially in terms of NTP server setup without internet connectivity. Novices may need clarification about model capabilities and instructions for configuring a device as an NTP server. Comprehensive documentation on establishing a local NTP solution is not readily available.
analysis.user_expectations: The user seeks a straightforward, novice-friendly guide for synchronizing time across all modules without requiring internet access.
